newsitem.title: CHILE: Antitrust ruling, foreign buying boost Chile shrs.
newsitem.headline: Antitrust ruling, foreign buying boost Chile shrs.

text.p: Chilean stocks posted new gains on power holding firm Enersis' successful defeat of an antitrust suit filed by state prosecutors and with brisk demand from overseas investors, brokers say.
The blue-chip IPSA index was up 1.49 percent to 136.78 points, and the all-share IGPA climbed 0.82 percent to 5816.62 points in busy morning trade, adding to a nearly three-point rise on Wednesday.

The state Anti-Monopoly Commission ruled after the market closed Wednesday that Enersis was not violating antitrust codes by owning companies in all three stages of the electricity business -- generation, transmission and distribution.
Enersis was up two percent to 307 pesos and its power generation unit Endesa rose 1.6 percent to 320 pesos.
"This was absolutely an effect of the ruling on Wednesday," said one broker.
Brokers also cited continued overseas demand for liquid stocks in what foreign institutional investors see as a relatively expensive but reliable market.
"We attract investors who want stability and our neighbors are a lot more risky than we are," said one.
